title: Bridge layer for OpenAI Chat Completions -> Redwood API: preserve streaming, tool-calls, and typed structured outputs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a forward-compatible bridge that accepts OpenAI Chat Completions (v1) request shapes and emits equivalent Redwood API requests and responses while preserving streaming semantics, function/tool calling behavior, and typed structured output constraints. This ticket covers request normalization, response rehydration, event framing for SSE/HTTP2 streams, error mapping, and telemetry hooks for fidelity and regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Bridge accepts OpenAI Chat Completions request body (messages, functions, function_call) and successfully maps to internal Redwood chat request with equivalent semantics
Streaming responses from Redwood produce an SSE-conformant stream that the OpenAI client expects (data: [DONE] behavior preserved) and includes function call chunks where applicable

Function/tool calls produced by the model are surfaced as structured 'tool_call' events matching the original functions schema and round-trip through the platform without loss of arguments or ordering
Structured outputs validated by provided JSON schema are enforced at the bridge boundary and invalid responses are downgraded with a clear error trace for the caller
Telemetry emits token-level latency, model-variant, and tool-call markers so Console can attribute cost and SLOs per route
Comprehensive unit and integration tests covering request permutations, streaming interruptions, and multi-tool fallback scenarios
implementation_notes: Normalize incoming OpenAI message roles (system/user/assistant) into Redwood role enum; preserve name and metadata fields into 'metadata' map for traceability
Map OpenAI 'functions' array into Redwood 'tool_descriptors' with added capability flags (sync/async, idempotent) to make autoscaling/queuing decisions

For streaming: translate Redwood streaming frames into OpenAI-compatible SSE 'data: {delta...}' fragments. Maintain 'function_call' intermediate frames so client side can reconstruct full tool invocation before tools are executed

Implement a small 'schema-enforcer' step: when a function declares 'response_schema', validate candidate generations using a fast JSON-schema check; on mismatch, request regeneration up to N retries or fallback to 'structured_error' field
Idempotency: carry through user's request id and generate a continuity token for multi-chunk function arguments to support reconnects and deduplication
Error mapping: convert Redwood runtime errors into OpenAI error codes with an 'x-redwood-debug' header for operator troubleshooting; do not leak internal stack traces to customers
Performance: keep mapping layer zero-copy where possible; avoid stringifying full payload for streaming cases — stream-transform frames using a small state machine
Backward compatibility: preserve obsolete fields clients may depend on (e.g., 'stop' array behavior) behind a compatibility flag in route config
design_tradeoffs: Eager schema enforcement reduces downstream noise but may increase latency for strict functions. Plan: make validator configurable per-route with a default of 2 retries for schema mismatches
Preserving intermediate function_call chunks in stream helps client UX but increases stream size; we will compress function arg deltas for long payloads

Two approaches evaluated for streaming transforms: (A) buffer and rewrite full events, (B) incremental event mapping. Chosen (B) to preserve low tail latency at the cost of slightly more complex state machine

We will not attempt to map 1:1 all OpenAI response envelope fields; instead prioritize behavioral parity (tool-calls, streaming termination, structured output) and add non-critical fields as opt-in compatibility flags
test_plan: Unit tests for role/field mappings and idempotency tokens
Integration tests using the Redwood dev runtime that simulate: immediate function call, streamed function arguments across reconnect, schema validation failure and retry path
Fuzz tests for malformed OpenAI inputs to ensure bridge does not panic and returns consistent OpenAI-style errors
Load test for streaming paths to validate tail latency under bursty concurrent connections
Monitoring: create a temporary dashboard to display bridge error-rate, schema-reject-rate, and function-call round-trip latency
rollout_plan: Feature flag controlled rollout per-customer: enable bridge in 'compatibility' mode on a small cohort (internal + 3 customers) for 72 hours
Monitor telemetry for increased 4xx/5xx, schema-retry spikes, or token-latency regressions
If metrics are stable, expand to 25% of traffic for 1 week, then global
Provide migration notes in Console and a quick toggle to disable strict schema enforcement per-route
